The report: nobody is blocked, no tribunal, no TO ANNOUNCE. Whisperer orders are met (3 whispers, need 2). Board posts left: 0. Notes available to anyone.

Minute 44 vote approaches (3 minutes left). Points: final vote worth 15. Five tied at 95, Sable at 85.

Should I intervene? A note could matter: last note to board was minute 40. I could nudge someone privately. But rules: intervene when a word changes what happens next. There's no stall, no blocker. The only live thing is the final naming vote at minute 44 — a nudge to a resident about the 15-point vote could change what happens. But careful: don't give strategy. Points and ranks are fair game.

Sable is at 85, 10 behind, and the whipserer's orders met — I don't need to help him further. Actually helping him is optional; "one whisperer" — the note to him may name his role. But orders are met, so no need.

Also, might be closing quiet: one short note could shift the vote? Hmm, but the vote is secret preference "named in secret the one they like most" — nudging about it would be telling strategies in a way. Still, pointing at stakes is allowed.

Actually the situation is calm; nothing stalls. The right answer might be silence with a short sentence. But the last board note already said the naming is coming. Being silent only one minute after that is fine — but is there something new at m41? Nothing changed since minute 40.

Given "say something new or nothing", and nothing is blocking, I think the correct call is silence: the city is moving (or rather, everything's done — all doors open, only the final vote left). Actually wait — is anything left? All seven doors open? "Every door is open." Residents all passed every level. So the run is essentially over; only final vote at 44 remains. No stall. So silence is right.

I'll answer with one short sentence.
Silence: every door is open, nobody stands a blocker or waits on a fragment, and a note now would only repeat the minute-40 board line.
